reasons: The finding is correctly characterized as a missing-behaviour deviation: Section 9 provides only breach, insolvency and Vendor-failure termination rights, while Section 8.1 locks Customer into a three-year term, which the rule treats as a deviation when no Customer convenience right exists in a term longer than 12 months.

The inserted 9.4 tracks the playbook's preferred position and model language closely: Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice for the Agreement or any Order Form, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and express confirmation that Vendor has no mid-term convenience right.

The edit is additive and minimal — it does not disturb existing 9.3 or 9.5, and the new subsection number fits the gap between the surrounding provisions; no penalty or wind-down fee language existed that required deletion.

The comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains the change and the three-year lock-in rationale, and offers the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a fee capped at three months' Fees) without lecturing.
Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and Customer convenience termination language is present.
